newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech IPB sale decision may come next week - FinMin.
newsitem.headline: Czech IPB sale decision may come next week - FinMin.

text.p: Czech Finance Minister Ivan Kocarnik said on Wednesday that "partial" decisions on the privatisation of the country's four largest banks could come at next week's regular cabinet meeting.
This, he said, could include concrete decisions on the sale of shares of IPB a.s..
Asked whether these decisions would be on principles or on concrete steps of banking privatisation Kocarnik said: "I think it can be both."
"Basically, there is a consensus concerning IPB... so there can be also a decision made that it will be sold off," he told reporters after leaving a cabinet meeting.
The Czech National Bank (CNB) last week had proposed to the cabinet a broad plan to privatise the major state stakes held in the country's "Big Four" banks.
This included selling the state's 31.5 percent stake in IPB a.s. to a top foreign investor, a plan already endorsed by Kocarnik, but requiring cabinet approval.
Czech officials have confirmed Japan-based investment bank Nomura and Dutch ING Bank have expressed an interest in the IPB stake.
Kocarnik said on Wednesday that the state stake would be sold through a tender if approved.

IPB said last week that its top management had a "constructive dialogue" in a meeting with senior officials of Nomura discussing the sale of IPB shares, but said further decisions were up to the government and central bank.

Prime Minister Vaclav Klaus who has welcomed news of Nomura's possible interest in IPB, said on Wednesday he hoped new CNB material "would go beyond" the suggestions already submitted by the central bank, but he did not elaborate.
